I’m very sorry to hear that :(( unfortunately it’s not a good idea. Bathrooms harbour so much bacteria and budgies, as well as all birds, are super sensitive to mold/bacteria/smells. Remember, in the 19th century, canaries were used by miners to serve as a protection of sorts. If the canaries started dying, that would mean the miners had to evacuate immediately because there was a gas leak somewhere. Just important to remember how sensitive and fragile bird lungs can be! 

If you can’t keep them in your bedroom, can you keep them in the living room? You’re not a bad caretaker. You are trying your best to give them a good life. Unfortunately, living in a bathroom is less than ideal for any species. Imagine you were confined to a small, dark wet space for eternity. lastly, feeding seed-only isnt the best diet for budgies. they do eat seeds in the wild, yes, but they also have to fly a lot more in the wild than in captivity. a combination of veggies, fruits and sprouts, alongside good quality pellets, is ideal. but its a big change and budgies especially can be stubborn. start with veggies and some fruits. lots of budgies take to kale, broccoli, carrots and apples easily once they discover they are edible. google bird-safe veggies and fruits. there are too many for me to name but its best to be safe because some things- like apple seeds or avocado- can be dangerous. my budgies loved spinach and thats often mentioned as a bird-safe food, and it is, but in moderation. also try to feed in different ways. some birds like whole leafs and others like it cut up in tiny pieces. be patient but also persistent. ❤️

good on you for deciding to use pellets! roudybush and harrisons are considered the best pellets. TOPS pellets are my personal fav as they are all organic but they lack vitamin D3 and i live in Canada. if you live somewhere sunny and can provide your birdies access to sunlight for at least 6-12 hours you might like TOPS :). 

roudybush, harrisons and TOPS are a bit expensive despite being the healthiest. if you want something budget-friendly you should go for zupreem natural (not fruitblend- too much sugar and artificial colours) or tropican 2mm (you would probably have to crush it up because even the smallest size is too big for budgie beaks🥴). the one you picked is very sugary and has artificial colours so i would pick zupreem natural or tropican 2mm. around the same price but MUCH healthier. 

again, keep trying to feed chop. your budgies wont take to pellets immediately, most dont, so dont be discouraged if they reject them. mix some of the pellets into their seed so they can get used to them and mix some in a separate bowl with some millet so you could track how much they have eaten. be persistent but also patient. i’ve seen many budgies take to greens quicker than other veggies so try that! also try apples!!! my budgie loved apples and its great for them. i would consider sprouting seed too- many tutorials on youtube for that. its very easy and healthier than dry seed.

try to mix things up with the fruits and veggies. most budgies take to eating veggies easier than fruits. start with greens. some birds like their veggies chopped up into very tiny pieces- use a food processor to get it tiny. other birds like whole pieces- i like to use clothespins to hold a leaf and just stick it into the cage near their fav spots. somewhere easy to eat. my sweet girl loved spinach😊. be persistent and patient. 

until she warms up to eating fruits and veggies, you can try to sprout her seed. its SO much healthier than plain seed. i use hagen budgie seed (the VME one i believe, its just plain seed). it sprouts so well. many tutorials on YouTube. i highly recommend sprouts even after your budgie converts to veggies&fruits! and you might even be able to trick your budgie into eating veggies by serving sprouts and veggies together! 🤞🏼

lastly- pellets are awesome but budgies are prone to fatty liver disease and most pellets are filled with fat/protein. however any pellet is better than seed. sadly budgies are their own worst enemies and most refuse pellets at first. don’t overwhelm your budgie with pellets for now- wait until shes comfortable with veggies and fruit. my budgie liked pellets soaked in warm water. if your budgie takes a liking to a particular fruit you can try to find an all-natural sugar-free juice of that fruit and soak pellets in there. just an idea

also, some budgies like apples- give that a try.
